title: Meatloaf
subtitle: Classic American ketchup-glazed meatloaf
excerpt: Ground beef and pork mixed with egg, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire sauce, and aromatics, formed into a loaf and baked with a ketchup-brown-sugar glaze. The definitive American comfort food main.
sourceNotes: American meatloaf is documented from the late nineteenth century. It appears in Fannie Farmer's The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896, public domain) and in numerous twentieth-century American home cooking texts including Joy of Cooking by Irma Rombauer (1931). The ketchup glaze is the standard modern American version, widespread from the mid-twentieth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, slice, and freeze individual slices interleaved with baking paper. Defrost and reheat in a low oven or the microwave.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be assembled, covered, and refrigerated the evening before. Bake from cold, adding 10 minutes to the cooking time.

content.text: Meatloaf is American home cooking at its most direct: a large, well-seasoned meat mixture baked in a loaf pan and served in thick slices. The ketchup glaze caramelises as it bakes, giving the outside a sweet, sticky crust that contrasts with the savoury, moist interior. It is better the next day, cold in sandwiches.

Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Mix the breadcrumbs and milk together in a large bowl and leave for 2 minutes to absorb. Add the eggs, grated onion, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Add both minces and mix thoroughly with your hands until evenly combined. Do not overwork or the texture becomes dense.
Transfer the meat mixture to a lined baking tin or a rimmed baking tray. Shape into a loaf approximately 25 cm by 12 cm.

Mix the ketchup, brown sugar, and Worcestershire sauce together. Spread half over the top of the loaf. Bake for 45 minutes. Spread the remaining glaze over the top and bake for another 20 to 25 minutes until the glaze is caramelised and an instant-read thermometer reads 70°C in the centre.
Leave to rest for 15 minutes before slicing. Serve with mashed potato and green beans.

items.cause: Overmixed, or too little fat in the meat
items.fix: Mix just until combined. Use mince with a good fat content (20%).

items.cause: Not enough binding from the egg and breadcrumb
items.fix: Rest the meatloaf for a full 15 minutes before slicing. Soaking the breadcrumbs in milk is essential.

content.text: Meatloaf is the Tuesday night dinner of mid-twentieth-century America. It appears in Fannie Farmer, Joy of Cooking, Better Homes and Gardens Cook Book, and every church potluck cookbook from Maine to California. The ketchup glaze is the standard American version, though regional variations use brown gravy, bacon strips, or a ring of hard-boiled eggs through the centre. Cold meatloaf on white bread with yellow mustard is its own reward the next day.
